ingredients: 500 g large river or tiger prawns, peeled with heads reserved
3 stalks lemongrass (ta-krai), bruised and cut in 4 cm lengths
200 g straw mushrooms (het fang), halved (or oyster mushrooms)
2 tbsp nam prik pao (roasted chilli paste)
5 bird's eye chillies (prik kee noo), bruised
steps: Simmer the prawn heads and shells in the water for 10 minutes over medium heat, then strain to make a quick stock and return it to the pot.
Add lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves and simmer 3 minutes until the broth smells strongly of citrus.
Add the mushrooms and nam prik pao and cook 2 minutes, then add the prawns and cook just 2 minutes until they turn pink and curl.
Take the pot off the heat, stir in fish sauce, lime juice and bruised chillies, and taste for a hot-sour-salty balance.
Ladle into bowls, scatter coriander and serve with steamed jasmine rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g boneless chicken thigh, sliced thin
150 g oyster or straw mushrooms, torn
4 bird's eye chillies, bruised, and coriander to garnish
steps: Bring coconut milk and stock to a gentle simmer with galangal, lemongrass and lime leaves for 5 minutes; do not let it boil hard or it will split.
Add the chicken and simmer 8–10 minutes until cooked through with no pink inside.
Add mushrooms, fish sauce and palm sugar and cook 2 minutes more.
Off the heat, stir in lime juice and chillies, then garnish with coriander and serve with jasmine rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 tbsp green curry paste (prik gaeng keow wan)
400 ml coconut milk, top cream separated
6 Thai round eggplants (makhuea pro), quartered (or 1 small aubergine, cubed)
1 large red chilli, sliced on the diagonal
steps: Heat 100 ml of the thick coconut cream in a wok over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until the oil separates and bubbles at the edges.
Fry the curry paste in the cracked cream for 2 minutes until very fragrant, then add the chicken and stir until coated and opaque.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk and water, bring to a simmer, add both eggplants and cook 8 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the eggplant tender.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar, add lime leaves and chilli, simmer 1 minute, then stir in the basil off the heat.
Serve with jasmine rice or khanom jeen rice noodles.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g pork shoulder or chicken, sliced thin
3 tbsp red curry paste (prik gaeng phed)
150 g bamboo shoots (normai), sliced and rinsed
steps: Crack 100 ml thick coconut cream in a wok over medium heat until oily, then fry the red curry paste 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the meat and stir-fry 2 minutes to coat, then add remaining coconut milk and water.
Add bamboo shoots and eggplant and simmer 10 minutes until the meat is cooked through and vegetables are tender.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar, add lime leaves and basil, and serve with jasmine rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Gaeng Phed Ped Yang (Red Curry with Roast Duck)

ingredients: 1/2 Chinese roast duck (about 600 g), deboned and sliced
200 g fresh pineapple, cut in chunks
100 g seedless grapes or lychees, optional
5 makrut lime leaves and 1 handful Thai basil
steps: Crack 100 ml coconut cream in a wok over medium heat, then fry the curry paste 2 minutes until fragrant and oily.
Add the rest of the coconut milk and the stock and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add pineapple, tomatoes and grapes and simmer 4 minutes, then add the duck and heat 3 minutes until piping hot.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar so it is rich, salty and slightly sweet, then add lime leaves and basil and serve with jasmine rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g beef sirloin or pork loin, sliced thin
250 ml coconut milk plus 3 tbsp thick cream to finish
8 makrut lime leaves, very finely shredded
steps: Simmer half the coconut milk in a wok over medium heat until the oil separates, then fry the panang paste 2 minutes until dark and fragrant.
Add the meat and stir 2–3 minutes until just cooked through.
Add the remaining coconut milk, peanuts, fish sauce and palm sugar and simmer 3 minutes until the sauce is thick and clings to the meat.
Stir in most of the shredded lime leaves and basil, then plate and drizzle with the thick cream, red chilli and remaining lime leaf. Serve with jasmine rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g beef chuck or bone-in chicken legs, cut large
400 g waxy potatoes, cut in chunks
2 cardamom pods, 1 cinnamon stick and 2 bay leaves, toasted
steps: Simmer the beef in 600 ml coconut milk with the toasted spices over low heat, covered, for 90 minutes until tender (chicken needs 35 minutes).
In a separate wok, crack the remaining 200 ml coconut cream until oily and fry the curry paste 3 minutes until deep red and aromatic.
Stir the fried paste into the meat pot with potatoes, shallots and peanuts and simmer 25 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Season with tamarind, fish sauce and palm sugar for a sweet-sour-salty finish and simmer 5 minutes more.
Serve with jasmine rice and a side of ajad cucumber relish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g bone-in chicken thighs, cut in pieces
3 tbsp yellow curry paste (prik gaeng kari)
2 tbsp crispy fried shallots to garnish
steps: Crack 150 ml coconut cream over medium heat until oily, then fry the curry paste and curry powder 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir to coat, then add remaining coconut milk and potatoes.
Simmer gently 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the potatoes are soft, adding the onion for the last 5 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar, top with fried shallots and serve with rice and ajad cucumber relish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g pork or chicken, sliced thin
100 g long beans, cut in 4 cm lengths
3 sprigs green peppercorns, fresh or brined
5 makrut lime leaves and 1 handful holy basil (kra pao)
steps: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and fry the curry paste and krachai 2 minutes until fragrant; this curry uses no coconut milk.
Add the meat and stir until the outside changes colour, then pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Add eggplant, long beans, baby corn and green peppercorns and simmer 8 minutes until the meat is cooked and vegetables just tender.
Season with fish sauce, add lime leaves and holy basil, and serve hot and fiery with jasmine rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g prawns, peeled (keep 4 for the paste)
3 tbsp gaeng som paste (dried chilli, shallot, garlic, shrimp paste)
200 g green papaya, cut in batons
150 g cha-om omelette squares or Chinese cabbage
steps: Pound the 4 reserved prawns into the curry paste until smooth, which thickens and flavours the soup.
Bring the water to a boil, whisk in the paste and simmer 3 minutes.
Add the papaya and simmer 5 minutes, then add long beans and cabbage and cook 3 minutes until tender.
Add the prawns and cook 2 minutes until pink, then season with tamarind, fish sauce and palm sugar so it is sour first, then salty and sweet. Serve with jasmine rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Gaeng Kua Sapparot (Pineapple Curry with Mussels)

ingredients: 500 g fresh mussels (hoy malaeng phu), scrubbed and debearded
300 g fresh pineapple, cut in small chunks
steps: Steam the mussels in a covered pot with a splash of water over high heat for 3–4 minutes until they open; discard any that stay closed and remove the meat.
Crack 100 ml coconut cream over medium heat until oily and fry the curry paste 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the remaining coconut milk and the pineapple and simmer 5 minutes until the pineapple softens.
Season with fish sauce, palm sugar and tamarind, add the mussel meat, lime leaves and chilli and heat through 1 minute. Serve with jasmine rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 pieces mackerel or snapper fillet (about 600 g)
300 ml coconut milk plus 2 tbsp thick cream to finish
steps: Pat the fish dry, dust in rice flour and shallow-fry in the oil over medium-high heat 3 minutes per side until golden and the flesh flakes; drain.
In a clean wok, simmer 150 ml coconut milk until it splits and becomes oily, then fry the curry paste 2 minutes.
Add remaining coconut milk, fish sauce and palm sugar and simmer until thick and glossy.
Spoon the sauce over the fish, top with the thick cream, shredded lime leaves and chilli, and serve with jasmine rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g baby corn and 100 g angled loofah (buap), sliced
steps: Pound the dried shrimp, shallots, peppercorns and shrimp paste into a coarse paste.
Bring the water to a boil, stir in the paste and simmer 2 minutes.
Add the pumpkin and cook 6 minutes, then add baby corn and loofah and cook 3 minutes until tender.
Add the prawns and fish sauce and cook 2 minutes until the prawns are pink, then stir in the lemon basil off the heat. Serve with rice; it is peppery, not chilli hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Gaeng Jued Tao Hoo Moo Sab (Clear Soup)

ingredients: 1 garlic clove and 2 coriander roots, pounded with 1/2 tsp white pepper
300 g egg tofu (tao hoo kai), sliced in rounds
50 g glass noodles (woon sen), soaked 10 minutes
steps: Mix the pork with the pounded garlic, coriander root and pepper and a little soy sauce.
Bring the stock to a boil, drop in small balls of pork and simmer 5 minutes until they float and are cooked through.
Add the cabbage, egg tofu and glass noodles and simmer 3 minutes until the cabbage is soft.
Season with soy and fish sauce, then finish with spring onion, coriander and fried garlic oil. Serve as a gentle side to a spicy meal.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 small dried smoked fish (pla krob or pla salid), about 100 g, broken in pieces
5 shallots, grilled until charred and smashed
steps: Toast the dried fish pieces in a dry pan over medium heat 2 minutes until smoky and fragrant.
Bring the water to a boil with lemongrass, galangal, charred shallots and lime leaves and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the fish and toasted chillies and simmer 5 minutes so the broth becomes smoky.
Season with tamarind, fish sauce and lime juice to a sharp sour-salty taste, add sawtooth coriander and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g white fish fillet (snapper or featherback), cut in thin slices
250 ml coconut milk plus 4 tbsp thick cream for topping
100 g Chinese cabbage or noni leaves (bai yor), blanched
4 makrut lime leaves, shredded, and 1 red chilli, sliced
steps: Stir the curry paste, coconut milk, egg, fish sauce and sugar in one direction for 5 minutes until thick and smooth, then fold in the fish.
Line banana-leaf cups or ramekins with basil and blanched cabbage, then fill with the fish mixture.
Steam over boiling water for 15 minutes until set and firm in the centre.
Heat the thick cream with rice flour until it thickens, spoon a little on each cup, top with lime leaf and chilli, and steam 2 minutes more. Serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 whole sea bass (pla kapong), about 700 g, cleaned and scored
1 handful coriander and 1/2 Chinese celery bunch, chopped
steps: Stuff the fish cavity with lemongrass and place on a heatproof plate.
Steam over rapidly boiling water 12–15 minutes until the flesh at the thickest part flakes from the bone.
Meanwhile, mix garlic, chillies, lime juice, fish sauce, sugar and hot stock until the sugar dissolves.
Pour the sauce over the fish, scatter coriander and Chinese celery, and serve bubbling over a tabletop burner if you have one, with jasmine rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 whole snapper or tilapia, about 700 g, cleaned and scored
6 large red chillies and 6 garlic cloves, pounded coarsely
1 handful Thai basil, some fried crisp
steps: Pat the fish very dry, dust with flour and deep-fry at 180 C for 8–10 minutes until deep golden and crisp and cooked to the bone; drain.
Pour off all but 2 tbsp oil and fry the chilli-garlic paste and shallots over medium heat 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add palm sugar, tamarind and fish sauce and simmer 2 minutes until a glossy sweet-sour-hot sauce forms.
Pour the sauce over the fish, top with fresh and fried basil and serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g glass noodles (woon sen), soaked 15 minutes and cut
100 g pork belly or fat, thinly sliced
4 coriander roots, 8 garlic cloves and 1 tsp black peppercorns, pounded
1 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tsp dark soy sauce
2 spring onions and Chinese celery, cut
steps: Toss the noodles with oyster sauce, soy sauces, sesame oil and stock.
Line a clay pot with the pork slices, then add the pounded paste and ginger.
Pile in the noodles, lay the prawns on top and cover tightly.
Cook over medium-low heat 12–15 minutes until the pork renders, the noodles absorb the liquid and the prawns are pink throughout.
Toss with spring onion and celery and serve with nam jim seafood sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 mud crab (about 800 g), cleaned and chopped, or 300 g cooked crab meat
120 ml evaporated milk or coconut milk
1 tbsp oyster sauce and 1 tbsp light soy sauce
3 tbsp vegetable oil and 4 garlic cloves, chopped
1 onion and 2 stalks Chinese celery, cut
2 spring onions and 1 red chilli, sliced
steps: Beat the eggs with milk, curry powder, chilli paste, oyster sauce, soy and sugar.
Fry garlic in the oil over high heat until golden, add the crab and stir-fry 6–8 minutes, covering briefly, until the shells turn red and the meat is opaque.
Add onion and celery, then pour in the egg mixture and stir gently for 1–2 minutes until it sets into soft, creamy curds.
Add spring onion and chilli and serve straight away with jasmine rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g pork belly or hock, cut in chunks
4 coriander roots, 6 garlic cloves and 1 tsp white peppercorns, pounded
3 tbsp light soy sauce and 2 tbsp dark soy sauce
steps: Fry the pounded paste in 1 tbsp oil over medium heat until fragrant, then add the palm sugar and cook until it caramelises to amber.
Add the pork and stir to coat, then add spices, soy sauces, fish sauce and water.
Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer covered on low heat for 60 minutes.
Add the eggs and tofu and simmer 30 minutes more until the pork is very tender and the eggs are brown. Serve with rice and pickled mustard greens.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Boil the eggs 7 minutes for a slightly jammy yolk, cool and peel.
Fry the shallots in the oil at 160 C until golden and crisp, drain, then fry the dried chillies 10 seconds and drain.
Raise the oil to 180 C and deep-fry the whole eggs 3–4 minutes until blistered and golden; drain and halve.
Simmer palm sugar, tamarind and fish sauce 3–4 minutes into a thick sweet-sour syrup.
Pour the sauce over the eggs and top with fried shallots, chillies and coriander. Serve with rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 tbsp shrimp paste (kapi), wrapped in foil and toasted
To serve: fried mackerel (pla tu), raw and blanched vegetables
steps: Toast the foil-wrapped shrimp paste in a dry pan 2 minutes per side until fragrant.
Pound garlic and chillies in a mortar, then add dried shrimp and shrimp paste and pound to a coarse paste.
Lightly bruise the pea eggplants into the paste, then stir in lime juice, fish sauce and sugar to a sharp, salty, hot dip.
Serve with fried pla tu mackerel, cucumber, long beans, cabbage and blanched greens, plus rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 6 garlic cloves and 6 bird's eye chillies
100 g pork belly, simmered in sweet soy until glazed (moo wan), chopped
3 salted duck egg yolks, cooked and crumbled
steps: Pound garlic, chillies, dried shrimp and shrimp paste to a coarse paste.
Mix in lime juice, palm sugar, fish sauce and tamarind until the sugar dissolves.
Fold in the sweet pork, flaked fried fish and crumbled duck egg yolk.
Serve this rich royal-style dip with rice, fried fish and fresh vegetables.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g cooked jasmine rice, rinsed until grains are separate
1 litre cooled boiled water scented with jasmine flowers or 3 drops food-grade jasmine water
2 tbsp shrimp paste, 3 shallots and 1 tbsp palm sugar, for shrimp paste balls
8 small shallots, stuffed with ground dried fish and sugar
200 g pork, shredded and fried with palm sugar until dry (moo foi)
4 green chillies, stuffed with minced pork and wrapped in egg net
Cucumber, krachai and green mango slices to serve
steps: Pound shrimp paste, shallot and sugar, roll into small balls, dip in egg and fry until golden.
Dip the stuffed shallots and peppers in egg batter and fry in 3 tbsp oil until golden and cooked through.
Fry the shredded pork with palm sugar over low heat 15 minutes until dry and caramelised.
Place rice in bowls, pour the chilled jasmine water over with ice, and serve with the fried side dishes and fresh vegetables; eat a bite of side dish followed by a spoon of cool rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 tbsp vegetable oil and 4 garlic cloves, chopped
250 g pork belly, cut and simmered with palm sugar and soy until sticky (moo wan)
2 eggs, made into a thin shredded omelette
4 shallots, sliced, and 4 bird's eye chillies, sliced
steps: Fry the garlic in oil until golden, add shrimp paste and cook 1 minute, then add the rice and toss over medium heat 4 minutes until evenly coated and hot.
Shape the rice in the centre of each plate.
Arrange the sweet pork, shredded omelette, green mango, shallot, chilli, long beans and dried shrimp around it.
Serve with lime wedges and mix everything together at the table.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 litres water, 5 cm ginger, 2 pandan leaves and 4 coriander roots
400 g jasmine rice, rinsed and drained
3 tbsp chicken fat or oil and 6 garlic cloves, chopped
2 tbsp grated ginger and 2 garlic cloves, minced
1 tbsp vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp dark soy sauce
Cucumber slices and coriander to serve
steps: Simmer the chicken in water with ginger, coriander roots and 1 tsp salt on low heat 40–45 minutes until the thigh juices run clear (75 C); plunge into iced water and keep the broth.
Fry the chopped garlic in chicken fat until golden, add the rice and stir 2 minutes, then cook with 550 ml chicken broth and the pandan leaves in a rice cooker or covered pot 18 minutes.
Mix the soybean sauce, ginger, garlic, chillies, vinegar, sugar and dark soy for the dipping sauce.
Slice the chicken, serve over the rice with cucumber and coriander, the sauce, and a bowl of hot broth.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g thin rice vermicelli (sen mee), dry
150 g prawns, chopped, and 100 g pork, minced
1 tbsp juice and the zest of 1 som sa (bitter orange), or lime
100 g bean sprouts and 2 spring onions
1 egg, fried into a thin crisp net
steps: Deep-fry small handfuls of dry vermicelli at 190 C for a few seconds until puffed and crisp; drain well.
In 2 tbsp of the oil, fry shallots until golden, add pork and prawns and stir-fry 3 minutes until cooked through.
Add palm sugar, tamarind, fish sauce and orange juice and simmer 3 minutes until syrupy and sticky.
Off the heat, gently fold in the crisp noodles to coat without crushing, then pile up and top with orange zest, bean sprouts, spring onion and the egg net.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g beef shin or pork, plus 300 g beef or pork bones
2 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 3 slices galangal, 2 pandan leaves and 4 coriander roots
3 tbsp dark soy sauce and 3 tbsp light soy sauce
100 ml fresh pig's or cow's blood mixed with salt (traditional; optional, or omit)
300 g thin rice noodles (sen lek), soaked
150 g bean sprouts and 1 bunch morning glory, cut
8 meatballs and chopped Thai basil, spring onion and fried garlic
Dried chilli flakes, vinegar and crushed pork crackling to serve
steps: Simmer the bones and meat in the water with the spices for 2 hours until the meat is very tender; skim regularly, then slice the meat.
Season the broth with soy sauces and palm sugar; if using blood, whisk a little hot broth into it and stir it back in off the boil to thicken and darken the soup, then reheat until steaming.
Blanch noodles, bean sprouts and morning glory in boiling water 20 seconds and divide into small bowls.
Add sliced meat and meatballs, ladle over the hot dark broth, and top with basil, spring onion, fried garlic and crackling; serve with chilli flakes and vinegar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g fresh wide rice noodles (sen yai), separated
1 tbsp oyster sauce and 1 tbsp light soy sauce
4 leaves lettuce and sriracha (sauce prik Sri Racha) to serve
steps: Heat the lard in a wok over high heat, fry garlic until golden, then add chicken and squid and stir-fry 3 minutes until cooked through.
Add the noodles and let them sit 1 minute to char slightly, then season with oyster sauce, soy and sugar.
Push the noodles aside, crack in the eggs, let them set halfway, then lay the noodles over and leave 1 minute so they crisp; toss.
Serve on a bed of lettuce with sriracha sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g mixed pork offal (intestine, stomach, tongue), cleaned well
2 tbsp white peppercorns, lightly crushed, and 6 coriander roots
3 tbsp light soy sauce and 1 tbsp fish sauce
300 g dried rolled rice noodles (kuay jab sen muan)
4 crispy pork belly pieces (moo krob), sliced, and fried garlic
Spring onion, coriander and chilli vinegar to serve
steps: Blanch the bones and offal in boiling water 5 minutes, drain and rinse.
Simmer bones, offal and pork belly in fresh water with pepper, coriander roots and garlic for 2 hours until the offal is tender; slice the meats.
Season the broth with soy and fish sauce; it should be clear and strongly peppery.
Cook the rolled noodles in boiling water 3 minutes until they curl into tubes, divide into bowls, top with sliced meats and crispy pork, and ladle over broth.
Garnish with fried garlic, spring onion and coriander, with chilli vinegar on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g mung beans (split, yellow), soaked 2 hours
3 tbsp nam prik pao (roasted chilli paste)
5 dried chillies, fried, and 5 shallots and 4 garlic cloves, grilled
3 tbsp palm sugar, 3 tbsp tamarind water and 2 tbsp fish sauce
1 tbsp juice of som sa or lime
500 g khanom jeen fermented rice noodles (or thin rice vermicelli)
Banana blossom, bean sprouts, long beans and fried dried chillies to serve
steps: Simmer the soaked mung beans in water 15 minutes until soft, then mash half of them.
Pound fried chillies, grilled shallot and garlic, then fry in 100 ml coconut cream until oily.
Add the prawns and cook 2 minutes, then add the rest of the coconut milk, mung beans and chilli paste and simmer 5 minutes until thick.
Season with palm sugar, tamarind, fish sauce and som sa so it is sweet, sour and mild.
Serve the sauce over khanom jeen noodles with the fresh vegetables alongside.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g khanom jeen rice noodles (or thin rice vermicelli, cooked)
400 ml thick coconut cream, heated with 1/2 tsp salt and 1 tsp sugar until just boiling
300 g fresh ripe pineapple, finely shredded
4 tbsp dried shrimp, pounded to floss
2 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tbsp sugar and 3 tbsp lime juice, mixed
4 fish balls (look chin pla), boiled and sliced
steps: Heat the coconut cream with salt and sugar until just boiling, then cool.
Coil portions of noodles on each plate.
Top with shredded pineapple, ginger, garlic, chillies, dried shrimp floss and sliced fish balls.
Spoon over the coconut cream and the fish sauce-lime dressing, and mix well before eating.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 green mango, julienned (or tart green apple)
steps: Grill or bake the catfish at 200 C for 25–30 minutes until fully cooked, then pick out the flesh and pound or pulse it into fine flakes.
Heat the oil to 190 C and drop in handfuls of the fish; it puffs into a crisp golden cloud in 1–2 minutes. Drain well on paper.
Mix mango, shallots, chillies, lime juice, fish sauce and palm sugar into a sour-sweet-hot salad.
Serve the fluffy fish beside the mango salad with peanuts and coriander, and spoon the salad over just before eating so the fish stays crisp.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g glass noodles (woon sen), soaked 10 minutes
1 small onion and 2 stalks Chinese celery, sliced
6 bird's eye chillies and 3 garlic cloves, pounded
steps: Poach the pork in 100 ml boiling water, stirring, 3 minutes until cooked, then add prawns and squid for 2 minutes until opaque; lift out.
Blanch the noodles 30 seconds in the same water until clear and drain.
Mix chilli-garlic, lime juice, fish sauce and sugar into a dressing.
Toss everything with onion, celery, dried shrimp and peanuts while still warm, and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g beef sirloin or rump steak
2 stalks Chinese celery and 1 handful mint, chopped
5 bird's eye chillies and 2 garlic cloves, pounded
steps: Season the beef with a little salt and grill over high heat 3–4 minutes per side to medium, then rest 5 minutes and slice thin.
Mix chilli, garlic, lime juice, fish sauce and sugar into a dressing.
Toss the warm beef and its juices with the dressing, onion, cucumber, tomato, celery and mint.
Serve on lettuce with sticky or jasmine rice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 banana blossom (hua plee), outer bracts removed
3 tbsp lime juice plus a bowl of lime water to prevent browning
200 g prawns or shredded poached chicken
1.5 tbsp nam prik pao (roasted chilli paste)
2 tbsp fish sauce and 1 tbsp palm sugar
3 tbsp roasted peanuts or toasted coconut
steps: Slice the banana blossom thinly into the lime water, soak 10 minutes, then drain and squeeze dry.
Poach the prawns in boiling water 2 minutes until pink and cooked through.
Simmer half the coconut cream with chilli paste, fish sauce, sugar and lime juice into a dressing.
Toss banana blossom and prawns with the dressing, top with the rest of the coconut cream, shallots, peanuts and egg.

ingredients: 1 pomelo (som o), segments peeled and broken up (or 2 pink grapefruits)
3 tbsp crispy fried shallots and 1 tbsp fried garlic
steps: Poach the prawns in boiling water 2 minutes until pink and cooked; cool.
Whisk chilli paste, fish sauce, lime, palm sugar and coconut cream into a dressing.
Toss the pomelo and prawns gently with the dressing, adding more lime if the pomelo is sweet.
Top with toasted coconut, peanuts, fried shallots and fried garlic and serve at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g wing beans (tua plu), sliced on the diagonal (or green beans)
150 g prawns, poached, or minced pork, cooked
2 tbsp lime juice, 1.5 tbsp fish sauce and 1 tbsp palm sugar
steps: Blanch the wing beans 30 seconds in boiling water, then refresh in iced water so they stay crisp and green.
Mix 100 ml coconut cream with chilli paste, lime, fish sauce and sugar.
Toss the beans and prawns with the dressing and toasted coconut.
Top with remaining cream, peanuts, fried shallots and sliced egg.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 sour green mangoes (mamuang kiew sawoey or any hard green mango), julienned
1 tbsp lime juice (only if the mango is not sour)
steps: Toast the dried shrimp in a dry pan 2 minutes until crisp and fragrant.
Dissolve palm sugar in fish sauce and lime juice.
Toss the mango, shallots, chillies and shrimp with the dressing.
Top with nuts and coriander and serve at once with fried fish or as a side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g large prawns, peeled and deveined
1 tbsp nam prik pao (roasted chilli paste)
1 handful mint leaves and 3 bird's eye chillies, sliced
steps: Grill or blanch the prawns 2–3 minutes until just pink and cooked through.
Whisk chilli paste, lime juice, fish sauce and sugar into a dressing.
Toss the warm prawns with the dressing, lemongrass, shallots, lime leaves and chillies.
Fold in mint and serve with rice and fresh vegetables.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g very fresh sashimi-grade raw prawns, peeled with tails on, butterflied and deveined
10 bird's eye chillies and 4 garlic cloves, pounded
steps: Use only sashimi-grade prawns kept on ice; this is a raw dish and is best avoided by pregnant, very young, elderly or immune-compromised diners.
Pound chillies, garlic and coriander root, then stir in lime juice, fish sauce and sugar to make a sharp green dressing.
Lay the prawns on a bed of ice with slices of bitter melon and raw garlic.
Pour the dressing over just before serving, top with mint, and eat each prawn with a slice of bitter melon and garlic.

3 coriander roots, 3 garlic cloves and 1/2 tsp white pepper, pounded

1 tbsp arrowroot or mung bean flour
250 ml butterfly pea flower (dok anchan) water

2 shallots and 20 g ginger, diced small

1 tbsp fish sauce and 1 tsp sugar

200 g minced pork or chopped prawns

3 coriander roots and 3 garlic cloves, pounded
Fried garlic oil, lettuce and chilli-vinegar dip to serve
steps: Fry the pounded paste in oil, add pork, radish, peanuts, sugar, fish sauce and pepper and cook until dry and sticky.

ingredients: 500 g boneless chicken thigh, cut in 4 cm pieces
4 coriander roots, 4 garlic cloves and 1 tsp white pepper, pounded
2 tbsp oyster sauce and 1 tbsp light soy sauce
1 tbsp sugar and 2 tbsp coconut milk
Sweet dark soy and sesame dipping sauce to serve

800 ml coconut milk, 200 ml thick top cream separated
2 tsp curry powder and 1 tsp ground turmeric
4 dried long chillies, toasted, plus 2 black cardamom pods (luk krawan)
2 tbsp fish sauce and 1 tbsp palm sugar
To serve: pickled mustard greens (pak kad dong), sliced shallots, lime wedges, roasted chilli paste in oil
steps: Toast the dried chillies and cardamom in a dry pan for 1 minute, pound to a coarse powder and mix with the curry paste, curry powder and turmeric.

2 tbsp dried kapok flowers (dok ngiao), soaked; omit if unavailable

Add the minced pork and stir-fry for 3 minutes until no longer pink, then add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until they collapse.

ingredients: 1 kg pork belly and shoulder, cut into 4 cm chunks
4 tbsp hang lay curry paste (dried chilli, lemongrass, galangal, shallot, garlic, shrimp paste)
2 tsp hang lay powder (Burmese-style masala), or garam masala

Add the water, tamarind, palm sugar and fish sauce, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 1 hour.

ingredients: 1 tsp sugar and ½ tsp salt
100 g butter or margarine, plus oil for soaking the dough
sweetened condensed milk and sugar to drizzle
steps: Knead flour, 1 egg, sugar, salt and water into a soft, smooth dough, divide into 4 balls, coat well in oil and rest at least 2 hours.
Stretch each ball on an oiled surface until paper-thin.
Melt butter on a hot griddle over medium heat, lay the roti down, crack an egg in the centre, spread it and add banana slices, then fold the edges over into a square.
Fry 2–3 minutes per side until golden and crisp and the egg is set.
Cut into squares and drizzle with condensed milk and a sprinkle of sugar.

steps: Fry the shallots and garlic separately in the oil over medium heat for 5–7 minutes until golden; fry the chillies for 30 seconds until darkened (not burnt) and the dried shrimp 1 minute; drain, keeping the oil.
Toast the shrimp paste in a dry pan 1 minute, then blend everything fried with the shrimp paste and 4 tbsp of the oil into a paste.
Return the paste to the pan with the remaining oil, add tamarind, palm sugar and fish sauce and cook on low heat 10 minutes, stirring, until dark red, jammy and sweet-salty-sour.
Cool and store in a jar in the fridge; use for tom yum, stir-fries and on rice.

steps: Combine fish sauce, chillies and garlic in a small bowl.
Add the lime juice and let stand 5 minutes; spoon sparingly over rice, fried eggs and fried rice.

steps: Pound the chillies, garlic and coriander roots to a rough paste in a mortar.
Add lime juice, fish sauce and sugar and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Stir in the coriander leaves and serve with grilled seafood; the sauce should be sharply sour, salty and hot.

ingredients: 1 cucumber, quartered lengthwise and thinly sliced
steps: Simmer vinegar, sugar, salt and water for 2–3 minutes until the sugar dissolves; cool completely.
Combine cucumber, shallots and chilli in a bowl.
Pour the cooled syrup over, top with coriander and serve with satay, pork toast or curry puffs.

ingredients: 300 g glutinous rice (khao niao), soaked 4 hours or overnight
1 tsp rice flour mixed with 2 tbsp water
2 ripe mangoes (nam dok mai variety if possible), peeled and sliced
1 tbsp toasted mung beans or sesame seeds
steps: Drain the rice and steam it in a muslin-lined steamer over boiling water for 25 minutes until translucent and tender.
Meanwhile heat 300 ml coconut milk with the sugar, ¾ tsp salt and pandan until dissolved, without boiling.
Pour the hot coconut mixture over the hot rice, stir, cover and leave 20 minutes to absorb.
Simmer the remaining coconut milk with ¼ tsp salt and the rice-flour slurry for 1 minute until slightly thick for the topping.
Serve the rice with mango slices, a spoon of salty coconut cream and a scatter of crisp mung beans.

ingredients: 3 tbsp chopped spring onion or sweetcorn kernels for topping
1 tbsp vegetable oil for the pan
steps: Blend 100 g rice flour, cooked rice, grated coconut, 250 ml coconut milk, 2 tbsp sugar and ½ tsp salt until smooth (base batter).
Whisk the remaining coconut milk, 50 g rice flour, remaining sugar and salt and the tapioca starch (top batter).
Heat an oiled khanom krok (or Danish aebleskiver) pan over medium heat, fill each cup two-thirds with base batter, then top up with the top batter.
Sprinkle with spring onion or corn, cover and cook 5–6 minutes until the bottoms are crisp and golden and the tops just set.
Scoop out in pairs with a spoon and eat warm.

ingredients: 50 g sugar plus 1 egg yolk for the shell
meringue: 3 egg whites, 150 g sugar, ½ tsp cream of tartar
50 g shredded young coconut tossed with pinch salt and 1 tsp sugar
steps: Whisk rice flour, mung bean flour, sugar, egg yolk and water to a smooth, thick batter; rest 20 minutes.
Beat the egg whites with cream of tartar in a heatproof bowl over simmering water, adding sugar gradually, until thick, glossy and reaching 70°C; then beat off the heat until stiff.
Heat a lightly oiled flat pan over medium-low heat and spread a spoonful of batter into a thin 8 cm round with the back of a spoon; cook 1–2 minutes until crisp and lifting at the edges.
Spread meringue on the crisp shell, top with foi thong or salty coconut, and fold into a taco shape; eat the same day.

ingredients: 6 small ripe bananas (kluay namwa), peeled and halved
steps: Simmer the bananas in water with pandan for 5 minutes until soft and slightly translucent.
Add the coconut milk, sugar and salt and heat gently for 5–8 minutes without boiling hard, so the milk doesn't split.
Serve warm in small bowls; the name means "bananas ordained as nuns" for the white coconut robe.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g water chestnuts, peeled and diced 1 cm
2 tbsp red food colouring or red syrup (or beetroot juice)
250 ml coconut milk with ½ tsp salt
syrup: 120 g sugar, 200 ml water, 1 pandan leaf
crushed ice and jackfruit strips to serve
steps: Soak the water chestnut dice in the red colouring mixed with 100 ml water for 10 minutes until deep pink; drain.
Toss in tapioca starch until evenly coated, shaking off excess.
Boil in plenty of water for 2–3 minutes until they float and the coating is clear, then plunge into iced water.
Simmer sugar, water and pandan 5 minutes for syrup and cool.
Serve the "crispy rubies" in bowls with syrup, salted coconut milk, jackfruit and crushed ice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g steamed taro or pumpkin, mashed (for colour), or 3 tbsp pandan juice
80 g palm sugar and 30 g sugar
steps: Knead the glutinous rice flour with mashed taro or pumpkin and water into a soft, pliable dough.
Roll into small 1.5 cm balls.
Boil in plenty of water 3–4 minutes until they float, then 1 minute more; transfer to cold water.
Heat coconut milk, water, palm sugar, sugar, salt and pandan until dissolved, add the balls and warm through 2 minutes.
Serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 ml pandan juice (blended pandan leaves, strained)
steps: Dissolve sugar in coconut milk with salt over low heat and cool; whisk in the flours until smooth.
Divide the batter in half and stir pandan juice into one half (green) and an equal amount of water into the other (white).
Oil a 20 cm tin and steam it empty 5 minutes, then pour in a thin 5 mm layer of green batter and steam 5–6 minutes until set.
Repeat alternating colours, steaming each layer until set, for 9 layers, finishing with green; steam the last layer 15 minutes.
Cool completely (at least 3 hours) before cutting with an oiled knife so the layers peel apart.

ingredients: green layer: 80 g rice flour, 2 tbsp arrowroot or tapioca, 150 g palm sugar, 300 ml pandan juice
white topping: 2 tbsp rice flour, 1 tbsp tapioca starch, 300 ml coconut milk, ½ tsp salt
steps: Warm the cups in a steamer for 5 minutes.
Dissolve palm sugar in the pandan juice, whisk in rice flour and arrowroot until smooth, and fill the cups halfway.
Steam over high heat for 8–10 minutes until set.
Whisk the topping ingredients smooth, pour a layer over each cup and steam 10 minutes more until the white top is set.
Cool before serving; the salty coconut top contrasts with the sweet base.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g grated fresh coconut, plus 100 g for coating
steps: Melt palm sugar with water in a pan, add 150 g coconut and stir over low heat 10 minutes until sticky and dry; cool and roll into small 1 cm balls.
Knead the glutinous rice flour with pandan juice into a soft dough.
Wrap each coconut ball in a thin piece of dough and roll smooth.
Boil in plenty of water for 3–4 minutes until they float, then 1 minute more; drain.
Roll in the remaining coconut mixed with a pinch of salt.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g very ripe small bananas (kluay namwa), mashed
100 g grated fresh coconut, plus extra to top
banana leaves for wrapping, or small cups
steps: Mix the banana, flours, sugar, coconut milk, coconut and salt into a thick batter.
Spoon into banana-leaf parcels or small cups and sprinkle grated coconut on top.
Steam over high heat for 25–30 minutes until firm and slightly translucent.
Cool a little before serving.

ingredients: 2 tbsp toasted coconut husk ash (traditional black colour), or 1 tsp activated charcoal powder
200 g grated fresh coconut mixed with ½ tsp salt
steps: Mix the ash with 150 ml water, let settle and strain to get black water.
Whisk the flours, palm sugar, black water and remaining water until smooth.
Cook in a pan over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, for 15–20 minutes until very thick, glossy and pulling from the sides.
Press into an oiled tin, cool until set, cut into squares and roll in salted coconut.

ingredients: base: 60 g rice flour, 2 tbsp mung bean flour, 150 g sugar, 400 ml jasmine or pandan water
top: 3 tbsp rice flour, 1 tbsp mung bean flour, 400 ml coconut milk, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp sugar
pandan-leaf cups (krathong), pinned with toothpicks, or small cups
steps: Cook the base ingredients in a pan over medium heat, stirring, for 6–8 minutes until thick and clear, then stir in the water chestnuts; spoon into the cups half full.
Cook the topping ingredients in a clean pan over low heat, stirring, for 5 minutes until thick and smooth.
Spoon the white topping over the base to fill each cup.
Cool until set, about 30 minutes, and serve at room temperature.

ingredients: 100 g black beans or red beans, soaked and boiled 30 minutes (optional)
bamboo tubes (lam) lined with banana leaf, or foil-lined jars as substitute
steps: Mix the drained rice and beans and pack loosely into the lined bamboo tubes, filling three-quarters.
Dissolve sugar and salt in the coconut milk and pour into the tubes to cover the rice; plug the ends with banana leaf.
Roast upright over a low charcoal fire for 2–3 hours, turning occasionally, until the outside is charred and the rice inside is fully cooked (or bake in jars at 170°C for 75 minutes).
Split the bamboo and peel back to eat the rice cylinder.

ingredients: 100 g black beans, soaked and boiled until tender
steps: Cook the drained rice in the coconut milk with sugar and salt over low heat, stirring, for 10 minutes until the liquid is absorbed but the rice is still firm.
Lay a spoonful of rice on a banana leaf, sprinkle with beans, place a banana half, cover with more rice and beans.
Fold into a neat parcel and tie two parcels together with string.
Steam over boiling water for 1½–2 hours until the rice is fully tender.
Cool slightly and unwrap to eat.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp tapioca starch and 2 tbsp mung bean flour
steps: Whisk the flours and pandan juice and cook in a pan over medium heat, stirring, for 6–8 minutes until thick and glossy.
Press the hot dough through a lod chong press or large-holed colander into a bowl of iced water to form short green droplets.
Dissolve palm sugar and salt in the coconut milk over low heat and cool.
Serve the drained noodles in bowls with sweet coconut milk and crushed ice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g tub tim grob (crispy water chestnut rubies)
50 g cooked sweet sago pearls or attap palm seeds (luk chid)
400 ml coconut milk with 80 g sugar and ½ tsp salt, dissolved and chilled
steps: Prepare each component and drain well (or use ready-made items from an Asian grocer).
Spoon a little of each into serving bowls.
Pour over the sweet salted coconut milk and top with crushed ice; serve immediately.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g split peeled mung beans, soaked 3 hours
natural food colours (red, yellow, green, purple)
2 tbsp agar powder dissolved in 500 ml water with 2 tbsp sugar
small chilli stems or tiny leaves for decoration
steps: Steam the beans for 20 minutes until soft and blend smooth.
Cook the bean paste with coconut milk, sugar and salt in a non-stick pan over low heat, stirring, for 15 minutes until it forms a dough that pulls away; cool.
Mould into tiny fruits and vegetables, push in toothpicks and paint with food colours; let dry 30 minutes.
Boil the agar solution 2 minutes until clear, then dip each fruit 2–3 times, letting it set between coats, for a glossy shell.
Remove the toothpicks, add stem decorations and keep in a cool place.

ingredients: 300 g puffed rice (khao tok) or toasted flattened rice
steps: Combine palm sugar, sugar, maltose, coconut milk and salt in a wide wok and cook over medium-low heat, stirring, for 15 minutes until thick and reaching soft-ball stage (115°C).
Add the puffed rice, peanuts and sesame and stir until evenly coated and starting to clump.
Press firmly into a lined tray (or wrap in banana leaf), cool until firm, then cut into bars.
Traditionally made for the Sart Thai festival in the tenth lunar month; serve with small bananas.

ingredients: 300 g ready-made grass jelly (chao kuay), or 50 g grass jelly powder with 1.2 litres water
100 ml evaporated milk or coconut milk (optional)
steps: If using powder, mix with water and boil 2 minutes, stirring, then set in a tray for 1 hour; otherwise cut ready-made jelly into cubes.
Simmer brown sugar and water 3 minutes until dissolved; cool.
Serve jelly cubes in glasses with the brown-sugar syrup, crushed ice and a drizzle of milk.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 10 duck egg yolks (or chicken egg yolks), with their membranes strained out
steps: Boil the sugar, water and pandan for 10 minutes into a light syrup, then keep at a gentle simmer.
Strain the yolks with the egg white through fine muslin, without beating in air.
Fill a foi thong cone (or piping bag with a tiny hole) and pour in thin continuous circles over the simmering syrup for 30–60 seconds until set.
Lift each nest out with a stick, fold into bundles and drain on a rack.
Repeat until the yolks are used; serve at room temperature.

steps: Boil sugar and water for 10 minutes into a syrup; transfer half to a separate pan and keep both at a bare simmer.
Beat the yolks until thick and pale.
Drop tablespoons of yolk into the simmering syrup and poach 2–3 minutes until set into flat discs.
Lift each disc into a small cup and pinch the edges into a 5-point flower, then spoon a little thicker syrup over; cool to set the shape.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 10 duck egg yolks (or chicken egg yolks)
steps: Boil sugar and water for 10 minutes into a light syrup and keep it at a steady simmer.
Beat the yolks until thick and pale, then fold in the rice flour.
With a spoon or a wet fingertip, drop small teardrop shapes of batter into the simmering syrup and cook 2–3 minutes until set and floating.
Transfer to a bowl of cooler syrup to soak, then drain and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g taro or mung bean paste (steamed and mashed)
4 shallots, thinly sliced and fried golden
steps: Blend the taro or mung bean paste, eggs, coconut milk, palm sugar and salt until smooth; strain.
Cook the mixture in a pan over low heat, stirring, for 10 minutes until it thickens.
Pour into an oiled 20 cm baking tin and bake at 180°C for 40–50 minutes until set, then grill a few minutes to brown the top.
Cool, scatter with fried shallots and cut into squares.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 small kabocha pumpkin (fak thong), about 1.2 kg
steps: Cut a lid from the pumpkin and scoop out the seeds; rinse and dry inside.
Squeeze the eggs, palm sugar and salt together with the pandan leaves by hand until the sugar dissolves, then mix in the coconut cream and strain.
Pour the custard into the pumpkin up to 1 cm from the top.
Steam over medium heat for 60–90 minutes until a knife inserted in the custard comes out clean and the pumpkin flesh is tender.
Cool completely, then cut into wedges.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Whisk the eggs, coconut milk, sugar, pandan juice, cornflour and salt until smooth.
Cook in a heavy pan over low heat, stirring constantly, for 10–15 minutes until thick and glossy and it reaches 80°C.
Toast or steam the bread until warm and soft.
Serve with the warm green pandan custard for dipping or spreading.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 tbsp Thai tea mix (cha Thai, orange-red blend)
steps: Bring the water to a boil, add the tea and simmer 3–5 minutes until deep orange.
Strain through a cloth tea sock, then stir in the sugar and condensed milk until dissolved.
Fill glasses with ice, pour in the tea and top each with 2 tbsp evaporated milk.

ingredients: 4 tbsp oliang powder (roasted coffee with corn, soybean and sesame)
100 g sugar or 4 tbsp sugar syrup
steps: Bring the water to a boil, add the oliang powder and steep off heat for 5 minutes.
Strain through a cloth coffee sock (tung tom) and stir in the sugar while hot.
Pour over ice-filled glasses and add a splash of milk if liked; serve black and sweet traditionally.

steps: Boil the tea in the water for 3–5 minutes and strain.
Dissolve the sugar in the hot tea and cool.
Stir in the lime juice and pour over ice; the lime turns the tea a lighter, brighter amber.

ingredients: 30 g dried roselle calyxes (krajeab), or dried hibiscus flowers
steps: Rinse the roselle and simmer in the water for 10 minutes until the liquid is deep red.
Strain, then stir in sugar and salt until dissolved.
Chill and serve over ice.

ingredients: 30 g dried bael fruit slices (ma toom)
steps: Lightly toast the bael slices in a dry pan for 2–3 minutes until fragrant.
Simmer with the water and pandan for 15 minutes until amber-brown.
Strain, sweeten with sugar and serve warm or over ice.

steps: Rinse the dried longan and simmer in the water with the pandan for 10–15 minutes until the liquid turns golden-brown and sweet.
Stir in the sugar to taste and cool.
Serve over ice with a few pieces of plumped longan in each glass.

steps: Boil the pandan leaves in the water for 10 minutes until fragrant and pale green.
Strain, stir in the sugar and salt until dissolved, and cool.
Serve chilled over ice.
